conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you during your stay. You’re here because of nausea and vomiting again, is that right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, exactly. It came on suddenly yesterday—white, mucus-like vomit. I tried my usual meds: Tigan through the J-tube, Ativan and Amerol by mouth, but nothing helped.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You were just discharged a few days ago for a similar episode, and you felt okay for about two days at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I was eating solids and felt much better. Then this hit out of nowhere. No diarrhea this time, just the nausea and vomiting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that fits with your history of gastroparesis flares. Your labs show your potassium is low—3.0—which we expect with vomiting. We’ve started IV fluids and 40 mEq of potassium to correct that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, that makes sense. I’ve been so nauseous I haven’t been able to keep anything down. Is that why I feel so weak?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, low potassium can cause weakness and fatigue. We’re correcting it now. For the nausea, we’re giving IV morphine and Ativan—same combo that helped last time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good, that usually works best for me. I just wish we knew why this keeps happening.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We don’t have a clear cause for your gastroparesis, but we know this treatment plan helps. For now, we’ll keep you on bowel rest—no food by mouth—for a day or two to let your stomach settle.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I understand. But how will I get nutrition?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll continue using your J-tube for hydration and meds. We’re not feeding through it yet, just keeping it clear. Once you’re stable, we’ll slowly restart oral intake.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And my other meds—like thyroid and omeprazole—should I still take those?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll continue your levothyroxine and switch you to IV pantoprazole for now, since you’re not eating. We’ll go back to omeprazole when you can take pills again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, thanks. I’ve also been anxious—this whole cycle is so frustrating.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I completely understand. We’ll keep your lorazepam available for nausea and anxiety. We’re also continuing your citalopram for depression.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your potassium is up to 3.6 this morning—much better. How’s the nausea?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Much improved. I haven’t vomited since last night, and the nausea is mild now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. We’re going to start you on clear liquids—water, broth, apple juice—and see how you tolerate it. Small sips, every 15 minutes at first.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll try. Should I still take my Tigan or dronabinol?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hold off on those for now. We’ll use them only if nausea returns. We’ve also switched your Ativan to oral form since you’re keeping things down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well—no vomiting, and you’ve kept down the clear liquids. We’re going to advance you to a soft diet: applesauce, mashed potatoes, yogurt.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That sounds good. Can I have toast or crackers?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, small amounts. But avoid fatty, spicy, or fibrous foods. We also talked about a 'small particle diet'—finely blended foods that are easier to digest.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve heard of that. Do you think it could help me avoid these flares?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It might. Some patients with gastroparesis do better on it. We’ll discuss it more with your gastroenterologist at your follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve eaten the soft foods and feel okay. No nausea at all.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Excellent. We’ll keep you on the soft diet tonight and aim for regular solids tomorrow if you continue to do well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Morning. You made it through the night without issues. We’re going to try a regular diet—small portions, though.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. I’m ready to go home. When do you think I can be discharged?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If you tolerate today’s meals and stay stable, we can likely discharge you tomorrow morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good to hear. Should I restart all my home meds when I get home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, exactly as before: levothyroxine at night, omeprazole, Tigan and dronabinol as needed for nausea, and your vitamin D twice a month.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And lorazepam for anxiety or nausea?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, 0.5 to 1 mg every six hours as needed. But try to use it only when necessary, especially for anxiety.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve done really well—ate a full meal, no nausea, vitals stable. We’re planning to discharge you tomorrow around noon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s wonderful. Do I need to follow up with my gastroenterologist?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you have an appointment with Dr. Evans in a week. They’ll review your progress and possibly adjust your plan.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the radiology appointment?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You have a scan scheduled next week—likely a follow-up on your hiatal hernia, though it’s small and probably not causing issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Final check—you’re still feeling well, no nausea?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No nausea at all. I’m ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. We’ll get your discharge papers ready. Remember: advance your diet slowly, stick to smaller meals, and consider the small particle diet.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. And call if the nausea comes back?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Use your PRN meds first, but if vomiting persists, come back to the ED. Otherwise, see Dr. Evans next week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Dr. Lee. I really appreciate your help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and we hope this flare stays resolved. Your husband is on his way up, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, he’ll be here in 10 minutes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. We’ll have the nurse go over your discharge instructions one more time before you leave.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Just to confirm—I’m to continue all my usual meds, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, exactly as before. No changes unless Dr. Evans recommends them.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the J-tube—just for meds if needed, not for feeding?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Correct. Use it only if you can’t swallow pills or need hydration during a flare. Keep the site clean and dry.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. Thanks again for everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing great. Take it easy at home, and we’ll see you only if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your discharge orders are signed. You can leave once your husband arrives and the nurse reviews your instructions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. I’m so glad to be going home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a quick final check—still feeling well?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, no issues at all.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. Discharge is official. Take care, and we hope to not see you back soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Dr. Lee. I’ll follow up with Dr. Evans and take it slow at home.
